correctness.rationale: Equation (1) is the independently reconstructed edge-indicator expectation: each focal-path edge is newly present iff all other descendant leaves disappear. Single-tip protection changes baseline expected PD by q times this HED score. Every binary n<=5 crown split is analyzed; n<=4 is 1+(n-1) or 2+2, both with a risk-independent maximizer. In the only exceptional n=5 split 2+3, score identities are Psi_AB=H-a+aq, Psi_C=H-b+bq^2, Psi_DE=H-t+(t-b)q+bq^2. The strictly positive Psi_C-Psi_DE=(t-b)(1-q) excludes D,E. Psi_C-Psi_AB=(1-q)(a-b(1+q)) yields an interior sign reversal iff b<a<2b, and exact threshold q=a/b-1. Witness H=4,a=3,b=2,t=3 gives q*=1/2. Direct 16-survivor-scenario exact-rational computations per focal taxon agree with all HED formulas; the universal proof is analytic, not finite experimental extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessed is strictly the exact smallest n for a change in the GLOBAL optimal single-tip protection choice under a rooted binary ultrametric tree and common independent risk, plus exhaustive n=5 crown-length criterion. Steel et al. 2007 give the general HED computation and HEDGE preservation gain, explicitly acknowledged and not rebranded as new. Their full text and the PLOS 2008 four-tip heterogeneous-threat example do not state or imply a uniform-risk sharp minimum. The 2021 Fair Proportion robustness article concerns a different index and extinction-reduction operation. No exact equivalent was found, subject to real residual risk of stronger or unlocated prior coverage.
residual_risks: The 2007 general rooted HED formula makes this five-tip result a finite topology specialization, so some unlocated published note could already give the same direct classification.

value.rationale: Natural global conservation-priority question: whether an optimal guaranteed-saved taxon remains optimal when all species risks vary together. The complete classification identifies the first possible failure at five tips and the exact comparative topology/length criterion b<a<2b; the witness has an explicit reproducible q=1/2 crossover. It separates homogeneous-risk sensitivity from prior heterogeneous-risk examples and provides a useful small benchmark for risk robustness tests. It is an exact structural boundary, not a textbook unit conversion, arbitrary numerical slice, or claim of a large theory extension.
